Hey , I just wanted to chime in here. Look into midwifes, birthing centers, and water-births. I think giving birth is more mental than anything. You need to prepare yourself mentally, and know that you can do it, and that you are capable of handling the pain. You are as strong or weak as you think you are, when it comes to birth. Your body will do what it needs to, as long as you are mentally strong. Don’t set yourself up for failure by automatically assuming you need pain management. A lot of it comes with serious risks to yourself, and to your baby. If you’re considering something, make a list of the pros and cons and then cross off every pro that only benefits you, and not your baby, and then see where you’re at.

I chose a water-birth, at a birthing center, with midwifes. 10/10 I could not have asked for a better birth. It was amazing. I loved it. It was painful, every birth is obviously, but it was on MY terms. No random nurses popping their heads in the room. No bright lights or loud noises. No one to forbid me from eating food or drinking water. It was just my husband, and two midwifes. And it was wonderful. The water provides A LOT of pain relief, too. It's painful, but it's manageable. You have to get yourself in a strong place, mentally. And I was like you, I started researching early. I wanted to make sure I did what was best for my baby, and not what was easiest for me. Also, I got to get up and take my newborn baby and leave for home 4 hours after birth, which was amazing. I wanted to sleep in MY OWN bed, and not have some mandatory stay in the hospital. Hospitals are NOT clean environments, and I just really didn’t want my baby to be there. I wanted to bond with my baby and husband at home ASAP and I’m so happy I was able to do that.

I think it's GREAT that you are researching now! I know you mentioned there were some complications with your birth, but often times complications are caused by hospital interventions. And if you still want to only give birth in a hospital, many midwifes have hospital privileges. Some things that really helped me.. I knew I wanted a natural birth, so I watched a lot of videos of women having natural births. Mostly home-births. I read a lot of birthing stories or talked to women about their births. These suggestions would help in whichever setting you decide to give birth. I highly recommend this book, if you can't read the first half, then at least read the second half of the book. It was unlike every other pregnancy/birthing related book I’ve ever read, and I’ve read many. I used this book, along with my own research, and all the knowledge I had gleaned over the years, and a couple of youtube videos (like a birthing class on youtube, just so my husband could know what to expect) to prepare for my birth. As for breastfeeding, it sucks for the first 2-3 weeks. It’s awkward and painful. It really is. Your nipples might even crack and bleed a little. But then, it just stops being painful and starts being wonderful. There is nothing else quite like it, and I feel bad for any mother who does not get to experience it. There are a million and one reasons why you should breastfeed, so I won’t get into that. Formula is comically sub-par to breastmilk. You can make it through the first couple of awful weeks when it comes to breastfeeding with the knowledge that you are doing what is best for your baby. It’s what got me through it. I’m really passionate about my little one, and I would not put my own convenience before my baby.
